title: Point Cloud Visualization (Shader Point Size Attenuation)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a large-scale point cloud viewer (bunny-like shape: sampled from a mixture of 5 Gaussian clusters).

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Point Cloud]
(1) Generate exactly 100000 points using hard-coded logic (5 3D Gaussian centers + random sampling), and store them in BufferGeometry.
(2) Use THREE.Points + a custom ShaderMaterial: point size must attenuate with depth (size attenuation).

[UI]
(3) id="colorMode": select the coloring mode uniform | height | distance-from-center (a select element may be used).
(4) id="pointSize": range slider with a range of 0.5–5.0, controlling the point-size scale in the shader.
(5) id="clipMin" and id="clipMax": clipping planes along the world Y axis (or equivalent logic); points outside the interval must not be rendered or must be discarded.
(6) id="showBBox": checkbox or button that toggles the display of the axis-aligned bounding-box wireframe.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  totalPoints: number,
  visiblePoints: number,
  colorMode: string,
  pointSize: number,
  clipRange: { min: number, max: number },
  boundingBox: { min: { x,y,z }, max: { x,y,z } }
}

totalPoints must always be 100000; visiblePoints must decrease when the clipping range is tightened.

Output a single HTML file that runs when opened directly in a browser.
